quotes.text: You can only enable Managed Payments for new subscriptions purchased through a Managed Payments Checkout Session. Existing subscriptions aren’t eligible.
Use an API version of `2025-03-31.basil` or [later](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog.md).
Set the `managed_payments[enabled]` parameter by updating your server’s call to the [Checkout Session API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md).
When a customer purchases a subscription through Managed Payments, it only authorizes Managed Payments to charge their payment method.
If you don’t specify the price’s tax behavior, Managed Payments adds tax on top of the price you set, by default.

old_evidence.text: You must accept the [Managed Payments terms of service](https://stripe.com/legal/managed-payments) in the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/managed-payments) before you can use Managed Payments.
During this preview, you can only enable Managed Payments for new subscriptions purchased through a Managed Payments Checkout Session.
To process a payment through Managed Payments, all the products the customer purchases must meet eligibility.

findings: Both full guides document converting an existing hosted or embedded Checkout integration, using payment or subscription mode, Dashboard enablement, eligible digital products and tax codes, and API version 2025-03-31.basil or later. Catalog products get a tax code through Dashboard or API; inline Checkout product data takes `tax_code`. The server sets `managed_payments[enabled]=true` at new Checkout Session creation. An existing subscription cannot be retrofitted, and the new integration route is documented separately (old raw lines 12–35, 47–65 and 116–164; new raw lines 9–47 and 74–100).

Stripe provides the MoR solution, and customer-facing Link acts as MoR at checkout and supports transactions and subscription management on its site (new raw lines 9, 194–200). The Customer-identity side effect is conditional: if an existing `customer_account` or `customer` ID is supplied at Session creation, Managed Payments updates that object with changed name or billing address needed for tax, even though the `customer_update` parameters must be removed (new raw lines 108–124 and 128–148; old lines 172–189 and 195–217). Neither identifier implies support for Connect charging. Digital goods, no shipping collection, and no Connect remain explicit.

The November guide still requires removal of many fields controlling Stripe-managed tax, payment selection, Adaptive Pricing, address updates, shipping, Connect, and post-sale functions. The subscription and one-time lists remain distinct, and the shared list omits different fields by mode. The three rows in the current summary flagged below are a captured documentation/authority change, not a wholesale change to parameter handling.

Subscription authorization in both guides is limited to charges through Managed Payments; another transaction outside the scope needs appropriate customer consent (old raw lines 234–246 and new raw lines 163–175). A new or redirected Session does not establish successful payment or an active subscription. The new prerequisites explain that a successfully paid Session references a Customer plus successful PaymentIntent or active Subscription, and November’s separate setup guide lines 398–410 calls for post-payment events, including asynchronous outcomes, rather than a success-page trigger alone.

Checkout testing covers billing addresses/tax and transaction detail inspection; sandbox does not automatically send purchase receipts and test purchases do not appear in the Link app. The test flow can manually preview receipts and exercise a Link account in a repeated Session; order-management testing in the Link app is explicitly a live-session scenario. The one-time test subsection retains the qualified phrase ‘if purchased’ for a Subscription, which is not a rule that `mode=payment` creates a Subscription (old raw lines 219–271, new raw lines 150–200). Price-level inclusive/exclusive tax behavior and the exclusive default plus Dashboard fallback remain dated documentation (old raw lines 273–279 and new raw lines 202–208).

Main route is wiki/index.md line 7 → wiki/stripe-index.md lines 130–138 and 788 → wiki/concepts/stripe-managed-payments.md lines 70–91 and 113–123. Concept line 83's broad ‘embeddable web components’ phrasing needs a Checkout-versus-Elements distinction for this adjoining use case. The existing source at lines 13–25 and 40–61 reflects the April guide, including undated ‘during preview’ and a list presented as current.
substantive_changes: April’s subscription table explicitly requires removal of `payment_method_options` (old lines 174–180). November’s corresponding table no longer lists the top-level field (new lines 108–115). The navigation/copy change alone does not establish blanket support for all payment-method options.

April’s one-time table explicitly requires removal of `payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage` and `payment_method_options.{payment_method}.setup_future_usage` (old lines 195–204). November omits both (new lines 128–135). The separate September 3 entry captured in raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-changelog-2026-11-07.md lines 15–19 explicitly documents use of those two scoped creation fields for Managed Payments Checkout Sessions. That supporting documentation is stronger than omission, without covering every payment-method subtype or authorizing external charges.

November drops the old standalone Dashboard Terms acceptance callout and the express sentence requiring all products in the purchase to be eligible, while preserving Dashboard enablement and product eligibility with eligible tax codes for each product. The old ‘during this preview’ qualifier is also removed while the new-only subscription restriction remains (old lines 8–29, new lines 9–22). This is a substantive change to prerequisite wording and framing. Neither omitted prerequisite wording nor the revised introduction grants mixed-cart approval or proves waiver of terms.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain April 23, 2026 evidence for Dashboard Terms acceptance, all-products eligibility in the old Checkout guide, and explicitly prohibited rows with mode scope. New capture still requires product eligibility and individual eligible tax codes. November separate eligibility guide lines 92–102 specifies each product sold with Managed Payments needs an eligible tax code, with direct sales, rights and full automation qualifications. November's separate mobile route retains all-products language (lines 43–50), which corroborates its own scope without extending it to new web behavior.

Preserve the April ‘during this preview’ framing as historical migration wording, alongside the same-era changelog's April 22 general-availability milestone in 39 business countries (raw/stripe-managed-payments-changelog-2026.md lines 8–12 and November changelog lines 32–36). November's more-than-80-country statement concerns indirect tax coverage, a different scope from merchant GA.

Document the dated Node sample versus November cURL, embedded form link slug now `ui=embedded-page`, numbered instructions and testing section relabeling as presentation/navigation, without Node deprecation, changed minimum API version, or a new embedded Checkout integration interface (old lines 24–29 and 47–164; new lines 13–18 and 35–100). The code samples with `success_url` do not establish an embedded-specific return contract.

Carry both captures' Managed Payments-only subscription payment authorization, default practice for unsent sandbox receipts, test/live Link distinctions, and configurable price tax behavior forward with dated provenance (old lines 244–279, new lines 173–208).

Retain April restrictions as historical, separate general subscription `payment_method_options` from named nested options, and preserve the explicit consent restriction for charges outside Managed Payments (new line 175).

Source line 19’s undated ‘during preview’ can be read as describing current product availability despite November’s unqualified new-only subscription rule (new line 9) and the dated April 22 GA evidence. The historical preview wording and GA milestone concern different claims. Clarify on reciprocal concept/source routes that Embedded Checkout is a supported route in this guide and not the separately described Elements integration. The generic MoR tooltip's Connect explanation at new line 104 does not override explicit Managed Payments no-Connect rows at lines 120–122 and 141–144.
unresolved_questions: The capture and targeted related excerpts do not establish whether the top-level `payment_method_options` accepts every setting in subscription mode, whether the September parameters are usable for every payment method or eligible account, or whether any particular session, instrument, transaction, tax outcome or authorization succeeds. November web guides omit the historical standalone Terms step without explaining whether it is still part of Dashboard enablement.

findings: Add the November guide evidence and preserve the April migration guide as dated provenance. Surface Dashboard, hosted/embedded mode, qualifying products with eligible tax codes, minimum API and server-created session in the main route (new raw lines 9–22 and 74–100).

Restore transaction- and migration-relevant omitted safeguards: conditional existing Account or Customer data updates, consent before charging outside Managed Payments, and the difference between session creation or a test redirect and payment/active subscription outcome (new lines 15, 116–117, 136–137, 150–200).
conflicts: Current summary line 19 says ‘during preview’ without scope. Its subscription and one-time tables at lines 46 and 57 present old unsupported parameters without dating them. September 3 changelog lines 15–19 positively support the two scoped `setup_future_usage` fields now absent from the November one-time removal list, but do not establish blanket top-level subscription `payment_method_options` support.
source_assessments.reason: A reader checking whether to strip a `setup_future_usage` field could follow the obsolete one-time removal list and miss the explicit later support, or infer consent from technical support if the consent boundary remains absent. An existing integration reader could miss the API minimum or confuse embedded Checkout with Elements. The current route surfaces the April evidence and current restrictions together without dates or the relevant reciprocal path.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/update-checkout, the November 7, 2026 guide requires an existing hosted or embedded Checkout integration creating Checkout Sessions in `payment` or `subscription` mode, Dashboard enablement, eligible digital products with eligible tax codes, and API `2025-03-31.basil` or later. The server sets `managed_payments[enabled]=true` on session creation and removes the mode-specific unsupported tax, payment, customer update, shipping, Connect, and post-sale fields. If a supplied existing `customer_account` or `customer` has a changed name or billing address, Managed Payments updates that object for tax purposes. Stripe provides the merchant-of-record solution and Link acts as merchant of record at checkout. New subscriptions must be purchased through a Managed Payments Checkout Session. Existing subscriptions are ineligible, and a session creation or redirect does not establish payment or active subscription. A Managed Payments subscription authorizes charges within Managed Payments, so charges outside it need appropriate consent (new raw lines 9-47, new raw lines 74-148, new raw lines 163-175 and new raw lines 194-208). The April guide shares the migration and consent model but explicitly included Dashboard terms acceptance and all-products eligibility. `source-stripe-managed-payments-update-checkout.md` lines 13-25 and 40-61 reflects April’s preview wording and older removal tables, and omits the consent and API requirements (old raw lines 8-35, old raw lines 116-217 and old raw lines 234-246).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/update-checkout, the documented removal lists substantively change: November omits top-level subscription `payment_method_options`, and the one-time list omits `payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage` and `payment_method_options.{payment_method}.setup_future_usage` (old raw lines 168-204 and new raw lines 102-148). The separate September 3, 2026 Managed Payments changelog entry, lines 15-19 of its November capture, explicitly permits the two named setup-future-usage parameters for Managed Payments Checkout Session creation. It does not establish blanket support for subscription `payment_method_options` or consent for charges outside Managed Payments. Date the old removal tables in `source-stripe-managed-payments-update-checkout.md` and retain that warning in the Managed Payments and changelog routes. November keeps the new-only subscription rule without April’s preview phrase and no longer repeats standalone Terms acceptance and the all-products sentence. Preserve the April prerequisites as dated, since omission does not waive terms or allow ineligible items (old raw lines 8-29 and new raw lines 9-22). Node.js-to-cURL examples, the embedded Checkout link change, test heading and formatting are presentation/navigation changes. API `2025-03-31.basil` or later, Checkout UI and server-side scope, sandbox-only testing behavior, and the price tax-behavior fallback remain documented, while successful payment, active subscription and consent remain separate (old raw lines 47-164, old raw lines 219-279, new raw lines 13-18, new raw lines 35-100 and new raw lines 150-208).
